title: Reproducing Simulation Results for the BCAT Model
author: Chung-Yuan Huang

steps.title: Install BCAT Repository and Dependencies
steps.instruction: Clone the BCAT repository and install the required Python dependencies.

substeps.instruction: Ensure Python 3.10 or later is installed.
Install dependencies using `pip install -r requirements.txt` (Required: numpy>=1.24.0, networkx>=3.0, matplotlib>=3.7.0)

steps.title: Run Baseline Scenario Simulation
steps.instruction: Launch the BCAT GUI and configure the baseline scenario parameters.

substeps.instruction: Set the following parameters using the left panel sliders: no-of-pioneers=5, clustered-pioneers=ON, bounded-confidence=50, convergence-rate=0.1, avg-of-attitudes=50, std-of-attitudes=10, avg-of-thresholds=20, std-of-thresholds=5, network-type=SWN, rewiring-probability=0.00, max-time=300

steps.title: Reproduce Sensitivity Analysis Data
steps.instruction: Generate statistical tables and figures from pre-computed sensitivity analysis data or re-run the analysis.

substeps.instruction: To use pre-computed data: navigate to `cd scripts` and run `python3 reproduce_table2_figs.py` (this processes 1,000-run batch results from 4 Excel workbooks in data/sensitivity_analysis/)
To re-run from scratch: use the BCAT GUI Experiments button with parameters from `test_scenarios/sensitivity_analysis_1000_runs.json`

steps.title: Execute Mechanism Decomposition Experiments
steps.instruction: Run controlled experiments (MD-A, MD-B, MD-C) to analyze opinion clustering and coordination failure.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to `cd scripts` and run `python3 run_mechanism_decomposition.py`
The script executes 30,000 total simulation runs across lattice and small-world topologies
Note: MD-A isolates coordination failure (FRI=1.0), MD-B isolates opinion clustering (no pioneers, GSI=0), and MD-C runs the full BCAT baseline
Pre-computed results are available in `data/mechanism_decomposition/` as CSV files

steps.title: Perform Finite Size Scaling Experiments
steps.instruction: Run scaling experiments to confirm robustness across different agent population sizes.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to `cd scripts` and run `python3 finite_size_scaling.py`
